note: Phase M1 scenario evidence for vendored Elisp packages (master plan 2026-08-21, section 5). Each package names its tracked source with provenance and a SHA256, the result of loading it unmodified, the features it requires and whether kg advertises them, the scenarios that pin its behaviour by input domain, and the domains it excludes with the scenario or feature id that records the gap. The four labels from section 3.1 are kept distinct: only scenario-green and supported are product claims. Snapshots in oracle/ are generated by `make package-oracle' against the pinned Emacs; the check (`make package-compat-check') regenerates nothing. A scenario pins an exact value, an exact condition, or a deliberately recorded divergence -- never a prose 'loads' or 'is supported' claim. Where kg answers wrongly today, the divergence is RECORDED here, not fixed: that is M2's job.

packages.name: s.el

required_features.note: (provide 's) is reached on load and featurep returns t, so the name is honestly advertised; that is the whole of what this label claims -- the supported contract is not complete (see exclusions and support_label).

packages.support_label_rationale: scenario-green FOR THE PUBLISHED DOMAIN s-core/ascii ONLY: every required s-core/ascii scenario agrees with the pinned Emacs 31.0.91 by exact value, condition, or handler-selection (the utf8 divergence s-upcase-utf8 is outside the domain and recorded, not fixed). Non-ASCII case folding, multibyte-string-p, combining marks and canonical normalization are explicitly excluded (see known_exclusions and supported_domain); kg has no Unicode database, so those answers are left unfaked. The 73-call smoke remains smoke only and is never claimed as support.

known_exclusions.reason: kg case-folds ASCII-only; non-ASCII codepoints are left unchanged, so (s-upcase "café") returns "CAFé" while Emacs returns "CAFÉ". Recorded as a divergence, not fixed (M2).
kg has no multibyte notion; (multibyte-string-p "café") returns nil where Emacs returns t. Recorded as a divergence outside s-core/ascii.
kg leaves non-ASCII bytes unchanged, so (s-downcase "ÉÀ") returns "ÉÀ" where Emacs returns "éà". Combining-mark handling lives in the Unicode table kg lacks. Recorded divergence.
kg performs no canonical normalization; (s-upcase "ß") returns "ß" where Emacs expands to "SS". Recorded divergence outside s-core/ascii.

supported_domain.name: s-core/ascii
supported_domain.summary: ASCII plus byte-preserving strings: every s.el operation whose input is ASCII (or a byte sequence kg preserves verbatim, including embedded NUL) is frozen against Emacs and agrees.
supported_domain.stop_condition: Unicode database would be required for correctness; not implemented. kg reports ASCII-only folding and leaves non-ASCII bytes unchanged, so the excluded families are loud divergences, not silent wrong answers.
